stage3.name: Back In Black
stage3.description: A macabre comedy about murder in a small town where the family running the local funeral home stands to make a killing. Christopher Walken is hilarious as the foul-mouthed mortician Clyde Mortimer, who bemoans the fact that people simply aren't dying like they used to. Weighed down by the sight of Clyde and his beloved wife Autumn (Jane Curtin) having to struggle so much in their golden years, their taciturn granddaughter Sam happens upon a potential means of reversing the clan's decline. Soon enough, people all around town are falling prey to “accidents” that help provide the Mortimer Family Funeral Home with a bounty of new clients. It's a hilarious and sharply observed satire from the longtime director of Trailer Park Boys, Ron Murphy. Ontario, 2026, 92 min. Cast: Christopher Walken, Jane Curtin, Ella Balentine. PEI Premiere.

stage3.name: A Long Winter
stage3.description: Following the extraordinary emotional resonance of 2023's All of Us Strangers, Andrew Haigh returns with a period drama occupying the liminal space between hope and acceptance. Adapted by Haigh and Colm Tóibín from the acclaimed Irish novelist's short story, A Long Winter follows Mike, a young man on the cusp of adulthood whose life is upended when his mother disappears during the first blizzard of the season. As the search stretches from days into weeks, the onset of winter becomes inseparable from the family's slow reckoning with the possibility that she may never return. Canada/UK, 2026, 117 min. Cast: Fred Hechinger, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Kit Connor. PEI Premiere.

stage3.name: In The Heart of The South
stage3.description: A crackling criticism of how the Canadian art world treats Indigenous artists, this psychological thriller stars Inuit actors from the series North of North. In The Heart of The South follows Yura Ivalu, the latest darling of the Toronto art world, whose virtual reality piece promises to blow your mind. Presented with a new opportunity to develop a film, she offers to lean into a traumatic story from her youth, which involves a friend who believed she was a shaman. What could be better than spending the evening with a mystery writer?  Spending it with two!  We are hosting a double book launch for Nancy Taber, author of Cove of Witches, and Katie Mac, author of Dunk River Murders. It’s going to be a great evening – you should come!
 
Date: Friday (Oct 16th)
Time: 7 pm
Location: Beaconsfield Carriage House
Tickets: Free, all are welcome

NANCY TABER writes mysteries including her debut novel A Sea of Spectres, which are inspired by Prince Edward Island history and folklore, with witchy women who make questionable decisions. She is a current Brock University professor and a former Canadian military officer. Nancy teaches fiction workshops at the French River Academie of Arts and Culture and facilitates with Writers Collective of Canada.
 
KATIE MAC writes noir, thrillers and westerns, all with a little bit of love and comedy. She co-wrote the Bell Fibe TV1 show Currie, based on the life of PEI-born wild west outlaw George ‘Flat Nose’ Currie. Katie received an Island Literary Award for her short story ‘The Key to Wednesdays’ and her debut noir novel, Ken’s Corner was published in 2024.
 
#AuthorEvent #ReadingWritingAndWonder #IndieBookshop
The Acorn Press Nancy Taber Katie Mac

incoming.eventName: Book Launch with Nancy Taber and Katie Mac
incoming.name: Book Launch with Nancy Taber and Katie Mac
incoming.description: A double book launch and evening of fiction set on PEI featuring A Cove of Witches by Nancy Taber and Dunk River Murders by Katie Mac. Nancy Taber writes mysteries inspired by Prince Edward Island history and folklore, and is a Brock University professor and former Canadian military officer. Katie Mac writes noir, thrillers and westerns with love and comedy; she co-wrote the Bell Fibe TV1 show Currie and received an Island Literary Award. Free; all are welcome.
